title: Kaibel, Epigrammata Graeca ex lapidibus conlecta (1878); RU «Греческие стихотворные надписи»; pilot: Attic sepulchral epigrams nos. 1–178
author: Anonymous verse inscriptions (ed. G. Kaibel)
size: c. 1,150 numbered poems (index runs past 1130); est. 6–9k lines
edition: Kaibel 1878 (public domain, archive.org epigrammatagraec00kaibuoft). For collation: CEG (Hansen), Peek GVI (1955), SGO (Merkelbach–Stauber 1998–2004), all copyrighted.
ru_evidence: No corpus translation found. CyberLeninka ('греческие стихотворные эпитафии перевод') returned nothing relevant. Only scattered items, e.g. in Black Sea corpora.
en_evidence: No English corpus translation found. Selections only in anthologies and studies (memory; not itemised).
other_translations: German: SGO (East Greek, with translations); Peek, Griechische Grabgedichte (1960), a selection
value: Inscribed epigram is the 'people's poetry' of Greece: grief, family, gender, status and afterlife beliefs. It is the indispensable counterpart to the Anthologia Palatina for the history of the genre. Russian readers have no corpus; strong appeal for students and the general public.
ai_feasibility: high: metrical, formulaic, well edited. Kaibel's 1878 supplements must be checked against CEG/IG; the commentary should flag restorations.
pilot_unit: Kaibel 1–178 (section 'Sepulcralia: Attica'; no. 179 begins 'Insularum et Asiae'), est. c. 1,000 lines
